correctness.rationale: For every unselected edge uv, d_F(u)+d_F(v)=1. Thus white vertices are independent and F is exactly all edges induced by nonwhite vertices. In a connected chain graph universal B1/A_p force a single surviving opposite-side center for one-sided white support, yielding only universal stars; two-sided white support forces the lone A_p-B1 edge, and residual independence gives exactly p=2, alpha2=beta1=1. p=1 complete bipartite degeneracies are explicitly deduplicated. All quantifiers and edge-count powers agree. Independently brute-forced 137,303,442 edge subsets across 1,049 profiles; matches all cases. Finite confirmation is not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural complete classification of a fundamental edge-domination notion on connected Ferrers/chain graphs. More than an optimization number: every PED-set is identified, its entire edge-size polynomial collapses to at most four simple terms for arbitrary large depth/part sizes, and a sharp necessary and sufficient singleton/DIM boundary is determined. The family contains arbitrarily large complete bipartite graphs with induced C4 and unbounded treewidth, outside some recent algorithmic classes; the result supplies a precise structural benchmark distinct from the known broad P6-free counting algorithm.
